verdict.summary: You create a Linear OAuth app yourself in workspace settings, and no review step is documented. Changing the distribution setting from private to public lets other workspaces install it. The only curated step is the optional Integration Directory listing. That review favours formal companies and has no published timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus a few hours of asset prep if you apply to the Integration Directory)
verdict.approval_wait: none (Integration Directory listing is optional, and Linear publishes no timeline for it)

gates.name: Private app (your workspace)
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own Linear account through your own app and Composio auth config.
limits: Distribution defaults to private, so only the workspace that owns the app can install it
Access tokens expire after 24 hours and must be refreshed
Request limit: 5,000 per hour per user or app user for OAuth apps

gates.name: Private app (workspace members)
gates.unlocks: Other members of the workspace that owns the app can authorize it. Linear has no separate test-user allowlist, so you add testers by inviting them to that workspace, or you switch to public distribution early.
limits: Only members of the owning workspace can use a private app
Every admin of the owning workspace can access the app's settings, so use a dedicated workspace

gates.name: Public app (installable by other workspaces)
gates.unlocks: Any Linear workspace can install the app. No review is documented for this. A listing in Linear's Integration Directory is a separate, optional, curated step.
limits: Customer workspaces on paid plans can require admin or owner approval before members install third-party apps
Directory listing is curated: Linear generally declines scripts, low-effort or vibe-coded apps, and hobbyist apps
Linear publishes no review SLA for directory submissions
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes (switch distribution to public). Directory listing: no published timeline.

steps.title: Create (or pick) a dedicated Linear workspace for the app
steps.detail: Linear strongly recommends a workspace used only to manage the OAuth app, because every admin of the owning workspace gets access to it. Make sure you are an admin of that workspace.
gotchas: A third-party guide (Clerk) says you must be a workspace admin to create OAuth apps. Linear's own docs do not confirm this.

steps.title: Open the new OAuth application form
steps.detail: In Linear, go to Settings > API and click '+ New OAuth application', or open the create page directly.
gotchas: The page is client-rendered, so field labels may differ slightly from what this guide describes.

steps.title: Draft the app details (optionally as a pre-fill manifest)
steps.detail: Prepare the required fields: developer name (the person or company responsible), OAuth client name, homepage or docs URL (an absolute http/https URL), and an optional icon URL and description. An agent can build a pre-filled create-app URL or a JSON manifest that matches Linear's published schema at linear.app/.well-known/oauth-app-manifest.schema.json.
gotchas: The client name must be 2-80 characters, must not contain the word 'Linear', and must not contain an http/https URL
Use an icon of at least 256x256 px. The description is capped at 1000 characters
Linear ignores unsupported query parameters, so check that the pre-fill actually took effect

steps.title: Set the redirect URI to Composio's callback
steps.detail: In the callback/redirect URLs field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config for Linear. You can register 1-32 absolute http/https URLs.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect_uri sent at authorize and token time must match a registered value

steps.title: Leave webhooks off unless you need them
steps.detail: Webhooks are optional. If you add one, the URL must be HTTPS, cannot be a loopback, private-network or linear.app host, and needs at least one resource type selected.

steps.title: Save the app and copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Save the app, then copy the Client ID and Client Secret into a custom Linear auth config in Composio (OAUTH2 mode). The endpoints are authorize https://linear.app/oauth/authorize and token https://api.linear.app/oauth/token.
gotchas: Store the secret securely. You can rotate it later in app settings without re-registering

steps.title: Choose the minimal scope set
steps.detail: Scopes are comma-separated. read is always included. Composio defaults to read, write, issues:create and comments:create. Drop write if issues:create plus comments:create are enough, and avoid admin.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, approve it in Linear, and confirm a token is issued and an API call succeeds. Then check that refresh works: access tokens last 24 hours and refresh tokens are on by default for new apps.
gotchas: Linear moved all OAuth apps to its refresh-token system on April 1, 2026, so your integration must handle refresh
A test with an invalid client_id did not return an OAuth error. It just showed a Linear page, so check the client ID carefully if authorization looks stuck

steps.title: Optional: enable app-actor or client-credentials mode for agents
steps.detail: If the agent should act as itself instead of as the user, authorize with actor=app (actor=application is deprecated). For server-to-server use, turn on client credentials tokens in the app settings. Those tokens last 30 days.
gotchas: Rotating the client secret invalidates client-credentials tokens. Existing user tokens keep working

steps.title: Let teammates test the private app
steps.detail: While distribution is private, only members of the owning workspace can install the app. Invite testers to that workspace and have them connect through Composio.

steps.title: Switch distribution to public
steps.detail: In the app settings, change distribution from private to public (described in a third-party guide as a 'Public' toggle next to the callback URLs) so any workspace can install it. No review is documented for this.

steps.title: Prepare for customer-side app approvals
steps.detail: Paid-plan workspaces can require an admin (or owner on Enterprise) to approve third-party apps before members install them. Write a short description of your app and why it needs each scope, so customers' admins can approve quickly.
gotchas: If an admin denied your app before, Linear shows later requesters the denial reason

steps.title: Optional: apply to the Linear Integration Directory
steps.detail: Fill out Linear's directory submission form, and send image assets to integrations@linear.app or link them in the form. You need a 320x320 color icon, a 320x320 monochrome white icon, and 1-3 designed showcase images at 1600x1000.
gotchas: Linear generally declines scripts, low-effort or vibe-coded apps, and hobbyist apps. It prefers formal companies
Linear wants designed feature images, not plain screenshots

steps.title: Wait for the directory decision
steps.detail: Linear publishes no timeline for directory review. Follow up, or request listing changes or delisting, at integrations@linear.app. Your public app keeps working while you wait.

requirements.item: Admin access to a dedicated Linear workspace
requirements.detail: Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for the app. A third-party guide says admin is required to create OAuth apps.

requirements.item: Developer name, OAuth client name, homepage/docs URL
requirements.detail: All three are required. The client name must be 2-80 characters with no 'Linear' and no URL. The homepage must be an absolute http/https URL.
1-32 absolute http/https URLs. Use the Composio callback URL.
Needed for installs outside the owning workspace. No review is documented.
320x320 color and monochrome white icons, plus 1-3 showcase images at 1600x1000. Built by a formal company.

scopes.effect: Broad write access. Included in Composio's defaults. Drop it if issues:create and comments:create are enough.
Narrow scope for creating issues. Composio default.
Narrow scope for creating comments. Composio default.
Full admin-level endpoint access. Linear says never request it unless absolutely needed, and customer admins are likely to deny apps that ask for it.
Agent scopes for app-actor integrations, used with actor=app.

blockers.symptom: The app form rejects the client name
blockers.cause: The name contains 'Linear', contains a URL, or is outside 2-80 characters.
blockers.fix: Rename it, e.g. 'Acme Agent' rather than 'Acme for Linear'.

blockers.symptom: You can't find or create OAuth applications in Settings > API
blockers.cause: You are likely not a workspace admin (reported by a third party).
blockers.fix: Ask a workspace admin for the role, or create a dedicated workspace you administer.

blockers.symptom: Users in other workspaces can't install the app
blockers.cause: Distribution is still private, which is the default.
blockers.fix: Switch the app to public in its settings.

blockers.symptom: A customer's member sees a 'request approval' screen instead of connecting
blockers.cause: The customer's workspace has third-party app approvals turned on (available on any paid plan).
blockers.fix: Have their admin (or owner on Enterprise) approve the app. Keep scopes minimal and explain why you need each one.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after about 24 hours
blockers.cause: Access tokens expire after 24 hours, and refresh is not being handled.
blockers.fix: Make sure refresh tokens are enabled and Composio refreshes with grant_type=refresh_token.

blockers.symptom: Server-to-server calls fail after a secret rotation
blockers.cause: Rotating the client secret invalidates client-credentials tokens.
blockers.fix: Update the secret in Composio and request new client-credentials tokens.

blockers.symptom: The Integration Directory submission is declined or gets no reply
blockers.cause: The directory is curated toward formal companies and has no published SLA.
blockers.fix: Polish the app and assets, and follow up at integrations@linear.app. Public installs work without a listing.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Linear OAuth to test quickly. Register your own app when you need your own branding or callback, a public app installed by customer workspaces under your name, actor=app or client-credentials agent modes, or your own rate-limit budget. Setting up your own app takes under an hour and has no documented review. Composio also supports an API key mode for Linear.

evidence.claim: Linear's OAuth docs tell developers to create an OAuth2 application and configure its redirect callback URLs.
evidence.quote: Create a new OAuth2 Application and configure the redirect callback URLs

evidence.claim: A third-party guide places the app under Settings > API, where a + New OAuth application button starts the form.
evidence.quote: Click + New OAuth application to add a new OAuth application.

evidence.claim: Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for the OAuth app, since every admin of that workspace gets access to it.
evidence.quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application

evidence.claim: Clerk states that a workspace admin role is needed to create and manage OAuth apps in Linear.
evidence.quote: You must be a workspace admin to create and manage OAuth apps in Linear.

evidence.claim: Required setup fields are developer name, OAuth client name, client homepage or docs URL, and at least one redirect URI.
evidence.quote: The person or company responsible for the application.

evidence.claim: The OAuth client name must be 2-80 characters, must not contain Linear, and must not contain an http/https URL.
evidence.quote: Must not contain `Linear`

evidence.claim: The homepage or documentation URL must be an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL and is required.
evidence.quote: The homepage or documentation URL for the application.

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs are absolute HTTP/HTTPS URLs, with 1 to 32 unique values allowed.
evidence.quote: Minimum items: 1

evidence.claim: Distribution is private (current workspace only, the default) or public (installable by other workspaces).
evidence.quote: Whether the app should be available only in the current workspace or installable by other workspaces.

evidence.claim: Linear recommends an icon of at least 256x256 px. The description is capped at 1000 characters.
evidence.quote: Recommendation: use an image at least 256×256px

evidence.claim: The create-app page can be pre-filled through URL parameters or a JSON manifest. Unsupported parameters are ignored.
evidence.quote: Unsupported query parameters are ignored.

evidence.claim: Webhooks are optional. The URL must be HTTPS and cannot be a loopback, private or linear.app host.
evidence.quote: The host must not be a loopback host, private-network host, or `linear.app`

evidence.claim: Linear publishes a JSON schema for OAuth app manifests.
evidence.quote: The published JSON Schema is available at

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint requires client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and scope.
evidence.quote: GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize

evidence.claim: The token exchange is a POST to https://api.linear.app/oauth/token with code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret, and grant_type.
evidence.quote: POST https://api.linear.app/oauth/token

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 24 hours and must be refreshed.
evidence.quote: The access token is valid for 24 hours and will need to be refreshed when it expires.

evidence.claim: All OAuth2 apps moved to the refresh-token system on April 1, 2026.
evidence.quote: All OAuth2 applications were migrated to the new refresh token system on April 1, 2026.

evidence.claim: client_credentials must be toggled on for the app. App-actor tokens last 30 days.
evidence.quote: You must first toggle on client credentials tokens for your OAuth2 app

evidence.claim: Scopes are comma-separated and include read, write, issues:create, comments:create, timeSchedule:write, admin, and agent scopes.
evidence.quote: Comma separated list of scopes

evidence.claim: The admin scope should be requested only when absolutely needed.
evidence.quote: You should never ask for this permission unless it's absolutely needed

evidence.claim: With actor=app, the app itself performs mutations. This is meant for agents and service accounts.
evidence.quote: actions performed with the received OAuth token will come from the app itself

evidence.claim: actor=application is deprecated in favour of actor=app.
evidence.quote: this was deprecated in favor of the behavior in `actor=app`

evidence.claim: Refresh uses grant_type=refresh_token. Credentials can be sent via HTTP Basic auth or as form fields.
evidence.quote: Use HTTP basic authentication by passing a Base64-encoded client_id:client_secret

evidence.claim: Secrets can be rotated without re-registering. Rotation invalidates client-credentials tokens.
evidence.quote: you can generate a new client secret or webhook signing secret without re-registering your application.

evidence.claim: The Integration Directory accepts external submissions via a form, with assets sent to integrations@linear.app.
evidence.quote: Fill out this form. It includes a sample page

evidence.claim: Directory assets are 320x320 color and mono icons and 1-3 showcase images at 1600x1000.
evidence.quote: Showcase images (1-3 max) 1600px x 1000px

evidence.claim: Linear generally declines scripts, low-effort or vibe-coded apps, and hobbyist apps for the directory.
evidence.quote: We generally do not accept scripts, low-effort/vibe coded or apps built by hobbyists

evidence.claim: No directory review timeline is stated. The contact is integrations@linear.app.
evidence.quote: reach out to integrations@linear.app if you think it should be included

evidence.claim: Listing changes and delisting go through integrations@linear.app.
evidence.quote: you can contact integrations@linear.app with the updates required.

evidence.claim: The directory page does not mention a privacy policy, domain verification, a security assessment, or a minimum install count.
evidence.quote: We recommend building applications using OAuth

evidence.claim: Paid-plan workspaces can require admin or owner approval for third-party app installs.
evidence.quote: Available to workspaces on any paid plan.

evidence.claim: If an app was denied before, requesters are told the reason.
evidence.quote: If the application has already been denied previously, Linear will let the requestor know and share the reason.

evidence.claim: OAuth apps get 5,000 requests per hour per user or app user.
evidence.quote: OAuth App       | 5,000 | User (or App User) | 1 hour

evidence.claim: A third-party guide says a Public toggle allows installation in other workspaces.
evidence.quote: toggle the Public switch to allow installation in other workspaces.

evidence.claim: A third-party guide says refresh tokens are on by default for new apps.
evidence.quote: Newly created OAuth applications will have the Refresh Tokens option enabled by default.

evidence.claim: The app registration page returned 200 but is client-rendered, so the form fields could not be confirmed.
The authorize endpoint with an invalid client_id returned 200 with no OAuth error parameters.
Composio lists Linear's default scopes as read, write, issues:create, and comments:create, with Linear's own auth and token URLs.

open_questions: Linear's official docs do not say whether non-admin members can create OAuth apps. Only a third party (Clerk) says admin is required.
Not confirmed whether a privacy policy or terms URL is needed on the app form. The manifest JSON schema was not fetched.
The exact UI label and location of the public/private distribution toggle come from a third-party guide, because the settings page could not be rendered.
No review timeline for the Integration Directory, and the submission form's questions are unknown.
Exact tiers for the dynamic rate-limit increase for actor=app workspace apps are not published.
The Nango guide mentions an Oct 1, 2025 refresh-token transition, which differs from the official April 1, 2026 migration date. Its meaning is unclear.
